[FACT] User recently took a break from social media.

[FACT] User did not log in to Twitter on their laptop during the break.  
[CHANGE] User is now trying to set limits for their social media use.  
[PREFERENCE] User is unsure how to stick to their social media limits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Congratulations on taking a break from social media and recognizing the impact it was having on your life!  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Setting limits for yourself is a great step towards healthier social media habits.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tips to help user stick to their limits include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Set specific goals and rules: Define why you want to limit your social media use and what you want to achieve.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Use website blockers and app limitations: Tools like Freedom, SelfControl, or Cold Turkey can block social media sites or apps during certain times of the day or for a set period.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Schedule social media time: Treat social media as a scheduled activity, just like any other task.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Find alternative habits: Replace social media with other activities you enjoy, such as reading, exercise, or hobbies.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Remove temptations: Consider deleting social media apps from your phone or moving them to a folder on your home screen.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Use social media intentionally: Have a purpose in mind when using social media.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 7. Track your progress: Keep a journal or use a habit-tracking app to monitor your social media use.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 8. Create accountability: Share your goals with a friend or family member.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 9. Be kind to yourself: It's okay to slip up sometimes.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 10. Review and adjust: Regularly review your social media habits and adjust your limits as needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips include implementing a "no phone zone" during meals, using social media analytics tools, and finding alternative ways to stay connected with friends and family.
